title: Understanding Your Metabolism: Facts vs. Myths

authorship.recommended_normalized_author: Healthy Weight Literacy Foundation Editorial Team

primary_question: What does the science actually say about how metabolism works, and which common metabolism myths are false?
reader_intent: Replace common metabolism myths (fast/slow metabolism, dramatic age decline, meal-frequency effects, metabolic damage from dieting) with accurate, cited science.
desired_reader_outcome: Reader understands BMR/TEF/activity components of TDEE and knows metabolism is stable from 20-60 and declines only gradually after, directly citing the Pontzer et al. 2021 Science study.

claims.proposition: A landmark 2021 study published in Science (Pontzer et al.) found that metabolic rate remains relatively stable from ages 20 to 60 after accounting for body composition, with a gradual ~0.7%/year decline after 60.
claims.article_location: "Myth: Metabolism slows dramatically with age" section
claims.recommended_action: Accurately represents the cited study by name, journal, and year; independently reconfirmed against the primary abstract during this audit. This is one of the corpus's best-sourced claims.

internal_link_recommendations.reason: Metabolic adaptation content connects to set point theory.

disposition_reason: One of the best-sourced articles in the corpus: correctly names and represents its primary source (Pontzer et al. 2021, Science), independently reconfirmed accurate during this audit. Well-hedged myth-by-myth structure with no unsupported specific numbers found. Only trivial editing needed.
